newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Big Three banks' rally slows on share offer.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Big Three banks' rally slows on share offer.

text.p: A rally for Taiwan's "big three" state-run banks showed signs of slowing at Thursday mid-morning as investors focused on Finance Ministry plans to sell some of its holdings in the three, brokers said.
With 65 minutes left, Chang Hwa, First and Hua Nan were up or unchanged as their prices neared levels at which the ministry had vowed to begin selling.

Chang Hwa, whose ministry target price is T$184 per share, was up T$2 to T$168. First Bank was unchanged at T$175 -- just below the ministry's target price of T$176 -- while Hua Nan gained T$5.5 to T$141.5, still well below its $188 target.

All three rose by the daily seven percent limit on Wednesday in a rally that has been led by the heavily weighted financials, spurring profit-taking on expectations of an imminent flood of shares in the market.
"Price-sensitive investors think the potential selling (by the ministry) may offset the rally on the Big Three," said Yuanta Securities analyst Henry Chen.

The bank's plan was to raise T$3.7 billion by selling off holdings in the Big Three holdings before July to ease a government budget deficit. Several papers carried updated reports of the plan on Thursday.

The ministry planned to sell a total of 20.55 million shares of the Big Three, including 8.87 million shares, or 0.54 percent, of Chang Hwa; 10.44 million shares, or 0.58 percent, of First; and 1.24 million shares, or 0.06 percent, of Hua Nan, officials said.
